THOUGHT: A 52‑year‑old woman has a 2‑year history of an immobile scar‑like nodule of the right upper eyelid that has been discharging pus for 10 months. There is no systemic illness. MRI shows a T2 hyperintense, ring‑enhancing lesion confined to the right frontal sinus; CT shows opacification of right frontal/ethmoid/maxillary sinuses and expansion of the frontal and ethmoid sinuses but no bone destruction. Sinus mucosa histology shows chronic inflammatory change (fibrosis, lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate, few eosinophils), and no malignancy. Taken together, these findings point to a chronic sinus process of the frontal sinus that has created a persistent draining tract to the skin of the upper eyelid (a rhinogenic cutaneous fistula). A frontal mucocele that became secondarily infected (mucopyocele) or a chronic frontal sinus empyema producing an external fistula best explains the chronicity, imaging (expansion and ring enhancement), and purulent cutaneous drainage. Other considerations include chronic cervicofacial infections (actinomycosis) or atypical mycobacterial/tuberculous sinusitis causing draining sinus tracts, and far less likely, a neoplasm that was missed on biopsy. The lack of bone destruction and absence of malignant histology argue against aggressive neoplasm or advanced osteomyelitis (Pott’s puffy tumor).

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Frontal sinus mucocele complicated by secondary infection (mucopyocele) with formation of a cutaneous (rhinogenic) fistula to the right upper eyelid
2. Chronic frontal sinus empyema/abscess with external drainage (frontal sinusitis with sinus‑to‑skin fistula)
3. Chronic cervicofacial actinomycosis involving frontal/ethmoid sinuses producing a draining cutaneous sinus tract
4. Chronic granulomatous sinus infection (atypical mycobacterial infection or tuberculous sinusitis) with chronic draining sinus tract
5. Sinonasal neoplasm with secondary chronic sinusitis and cutaneous fistula (less likely given negative histology)
ground_truth: Pott's puffy tumor with sinocutaneous fistula secondary to chronic sinusitis
